evidence.claim_scope: Faraday First Series contemporary published text, Section 5, presentation order versus observation order
evidence.limitations: Transcription/1839 republication, not independent handwritten diary. Publication explicit about editorial arrangement.

evidence.claim_scope: Faraday Second Series 1832 published first-person witness, paragraphs 183–190 on null or confounded long-wire/water effects
evidence.limitations: 1839 bound reprint; PDF image screenshot failed; inference limited to author's reported negative findings, not a raw independent repeat.

evidence.claim_scope: Faraday 6 January 1832 letter, edited transcription of proposal to lay wire at a pond
evidence.limitations: Letter evidences intention, not actual experimental success; editor's footnotes are separate secondary evidence.

evidence.claim_scope: Epsilon editorial notes from diary recording failed 28 December and January long-wire experiments
evidence.limitations: Footnote depends on source diary; not independently transcribed primary observations for every run.

evidence.claim_scope: Steinle 1997 analytic distinction between theory-guided ring experiment and later exploratory elementary experiment
evidence.limitations: Strong established prior scholarship; interpretation cannot be counted as MQR's new discovery.

evidence.claim_scope: CHSH 1969 original published proposal concerning inequality, detection bridge, experiment angles and calibration
evidence.limitations: Additional photo-detection assumptions; no automatic closure of all later experimental loopholes.

evidence.claim_scope: Freedman–Clauser 1972 January original author preprint LBL-392 and published summary contrast
evidence.limitations: Author source and rounded rates, but no original time-resolved counts; screening assumptions remain.

evidence.claim_scope: MQR founding seven-question comparison reconstructed in MQR 41 and MQR 44 from project records
evidence.limitations: Project constitution is normative internal document, not empirical proof of its philosophical validity.

evidence.claim_scope: MQR R61/R63 exact countermodels and R70 validated code receipts
evidence.limitations: Synthetic model mathematics; not an external physical experiment or new theorem.

evidence.claim_scope: Faraday Diary Volume I scanned 1932 first edited edition identified at Internet Archive/Open Library
evidence.limitations: Catalog/discovery only. Whole required 1831 Dec and 1832 Jan primary passage not independently visually read; Drive not held.

evidence.claim_scope: Faraday's Second Series numbered condition analysis distinguishing induced current and several interferents
evidence.limitations: Same source as E02, NOT independent corroboration; distinct evidentiary passage.

evidence.claim_scope: Royal Society Second Series manuscript PT/20/5 dated 21 Dec 1831, read 12 Jan 1832
evidence.limitations: Catalog is primary archival metadata on date; manuscript text/insertions not inspected.

evidence.claim_scope: 1832 original printed Second Series §§183–190 includes 1832 water/long-wire experiments
evidence.limitations: Source is contemporaneous printed text; PDF screenshot request failed; does not certify unmodified dated manuscript.

evidence.claim_scope: Epsilon editorial chronology dates 10 and 12-13 January 1832 experiments
evidence.limitations: Editorial note cites diary; original diary pages not verified. Shares underlying record with E04, do not add independent evidence count.

evidence.claim_scope: 1840 Faraday retrospective letter to Arago appears to confirm Dec21 authorship vs Jan12 reading
evidence.limitations: Only indexed extract examined; not independent original full PDF inspection.

evidence.claim_scope: 2015 historical science commentary dates First Series Royal Society presentation, draft and publication layers
evidence.limitations: Scholarly secondary account; web page reCAPTCHA prevented direct whole-text read this pass.

evidence.claim_scope: Faraday Second Series §231 and §242 critically withdraw evidential grounds for electro-tonic state
evidence.limitations: Second Series 1832 published source directly text-read; same document as E13 and original page screenshot remote-cache failure; does not prove permanent abandonment.

evidence.claim_scope: Faraday Second Series §§243–246 explicitly contrasts induced-current vs induced-magnetism accounts in rotating disc with dual magnetic poles
evidence.limitations: This is same contemporary article as E13/E17, not an independent replicated experiment or external validation.

evidence.claim_scope: Dictionary of Scientific Biography history says Faraday's 1832 abandonment of electro-tonic state was temporary
evidence.limitations: Secondary biography publicly indexed; full PDF image not inspected; existing history strongly cautions against permanent retirement language.

evidence.claim_scope: 1991 doctoral thesis historical abstract specifically treats evolving Faraday electro-tonic state
evidence.limitations: Thesis abstract/record only, not a full independent reading of dissertation.

evidence.claim_scope: Faraday first-person 29 November 1831 Phillips letter coins electro-tonic state and explicitly compares experimental and mathematical discovery
evidence.limitations: Edited scholarly transcription of original letter (SI D MS 853B), not personally checked autograph image; letter shows scientist's claim of influence, not objective superiority of experiment.

evidence.claim_scope: Faraday 1852 Philosophical Magazine reprint §3256 and §3269 revisits electro-tonic hypothesis, while distinguishing incomplete physical evidence
evidence.limitations: 1852 original article available as PDF extraction; image screenshot attempted but cache miss; quoted text verified, not handwritten/figure facsimile.

evidence.claim_scope: Maxwell 1855/56 original On Faraday's Lines of Force as printed in Niven collected scientific papers, explaining electro-tonic mathematical functions as provisional, not verified physical medium
evidence.limitations: Late 19th-century collected printed reprint, not 1855 manuscript; mathematics OCR unreliable and equations not visually source-verified.

evidence.claim_scope: Maxwell On Physical Lines of Force 1861–62 authored provisional mechanical analogy, electrotonic components, distinctions from empirical fact
evidence.limitations: Wikisource transcription and 1860s published papers, not independent physical replication; mechanical model not confirmed physically real.
evidence.locator: part II intro, electrotonic functions and recap

evidence.claim_scope: C.R. Nappo 2021 earlier philosophy of Maxwell analogies and physical-vs-representational distinction
evidence.limitations: Search excerpts support that topic exists, not full independent reading of PDF; avoid overclaiming detailed prior arguments.

claims.claim: Faraday 1831 First Series authored published account reordered results relative to actual discovery chronology
claims.rationale: Author states this rhetorical ordering; direct author source, not exact diary-run reconstruction.
claims.falsifier: Compare autograph submitted manuscript and journal printing for wording.

claims.claim: Faraday 1832 Waterloo Bridge experimental observations were confounded and did not furnish satisfactory induction results
claims.rationale: Contemporary author explicitly attributes galvanometer deflections to temperature, contacts, plate and water conditions; E02/E11 same source so not independent.
claims.falsifier: Original diary records or controlled modern repeat reveal a robust physically intended effect and distinguish alternative sources.

claims.claim: Faraday 1832 6 January letter demonstrates planning of pond long-wire experiment but not its outcome
claims.rationale: Letter first person states intention; later failure supplied as distinct editorial note.
claims.falsifier: Contemporaneous lab report shows conducted trial or documented different intent.

claims.claim: Faraday research shifted from theory-guided early ring to more exploratory condition variation
claims.rationale: Steinle established mixed-regime reading and source shows theory/perturbation/negative cases.
claims.falsifier: Full dated notebook reconstruction shows uniform unchanged hypothesis/test architecture.

claims.claim: MQR seven questions remain an appropriate broad research constitution, irrespective of local novelty-left scores
claims.rationale: Normative coherence and history of program; claims only fidelity to the program, not objective universal optimality.
claims.falsifier: Founding user text disconfirms seven-question reconstruction or source history.

claims.claim: Bell–CHSH 1969/1972 is a documented theory-guided experiment-design example under detection assumptions
claims.rationale: 1969 proposal and 1972 preprint give distinct temporally ordered plan/implementation, not loophole-free result.
claims.falsifier: 1972 original contradicts claimed geometry or measurement bridge.

claims.claim: Faraday example alone proves a universal law for scientific question generation
claims.rationale: Neither a single episode nor Steinle interpretation establishes universally generalizable scientific law.
claims.falsifier: Independent rival cases and a prospective falsifiable quantitative prediction would be required.

claims.claim: Current LIRA 1.0 scalar priority may discard mandatory founding evidence cases without constitution guard
claims.rationale: Counterexample: rank-only algorithm can deprioritize protected case even if essential; direct code-level design failure.
claims.falsifier: Existing code formally mandates all seven and protected Faraday under all weighting schemes.

claims.claim: Not all published Faraday signals count as verified intended physical target
claims.rationale: Second Series author distinguishes galvanometer deflection from satisfactory water-motion induction explanation.
claims.falsifier: Primary text shows those exact deflections were accepted as unambiguously target-generated.

claims.claim: Full 1831 December and 1832 January original edited Diary is available to the model and has been comprehensively audited
claims.rationale: Public edition identified but content-range visual/complete reading is unverified and no custody receipt.
claims.falsifier: Retrieve certified complete volume and inspect original dated entries, pages/figures.

claims.claim: Protect Faraday as active Q3/Q4/Q7 witness even though Steinle prior art lowers novelty
claims.rationale: Research-program coverage and contrast between guided and exploratory stages, not uniqueness of claim.
claims.falsifier: New founding constitution removes these research questions.

claims.claim: Preserve Bell as comparative control, not another long PR-box-only modeling loop
claims.rationale: Explicit documented protocol chain clarifies difference with Faraday; further local toy model has diminishing evidentiary novelty.
claims.falsifier: New model offers independent discriminating empirical evidence unavailable in established protocols.

claims.claim: Acquire complete Faraday Diary Volume I into 00_INTAKE before claiming the precise Dec/Jan sequence
claims.rationale: The missing dated primary episodes are exactly what can change historical causal interpretation.
claims.falsifier: Accessible complete and independently verified identical diary already held in Drive.

claims.claim: Keep cross-science conceptual bridge and paired measurement as distinct open questions
claims.rationale: Founding program explicitly separates symbol/experiment grounding and identical samples; current synthetic tests do not close empirical gap.
claims.falsifier: Original program or new verified empirical bridge closes open premise.

claims.claim: LIRA evidence quality and support ratings justify MQR 5.5 promotion
claims.rationale: Internal declared ratings cannot replace empirical validation, independence and competing accounts.
claims.falsifier: Independent evidence plus novel predictions/accepted cross-domain tests could motivate different evaluation.

claims.claim: Royal Society catalogs a Dec 21 1831 Second Series manuscript and a Jan 12 1832 reading
claims.rationale: Catalog metadata explicitly has both dates; archive item full text not yet read.
claims.falsifier: Archival PT/20/5 corrected catalog supplies another date.

claims.claim: 1832 printed Second Series describes later January field trials that cannot automatically be assigned to unchanged Dec 21 draft
claims.rationale: Print text + later experiments + archival manuscript date create a versioning question; exact moment of editorial insertion remains unknown.
claims.falsifier: Compare dated handwritten draft and final print; evaluate if date metadata or letter misdates experiments.

claims.claim: Faraday appended exactly paragraphs 183–190 on or after January 13 to the originally dated paper
claims.rationale: This exact redaction history is one possible explanation, but archival manuscript text/corrections have not been inspected.
claims.falsifier: Find original paper manuscript showing these paragraphs existed beforehand or a precisely dated edited version.

claims.claim: Original First Series rhetorical ordering equals actual experimental discovery order
claims.rationale: Faraday explicitly says narrative order differs from actual discoveries; this claim is contradicted in scope.
claims.falsifier: A first-person original text recanting or qualifying that direct statement.

claims.claim: Compare Second Series dated manuscript PT/20/5 with original 1832 printed paper before reconstructing a January causal sequence
claims.rationale: Chronological contradiction risks retrospective contamination; manuscript/print concordance is decisive.
claims.falsifier: Collated manuscript already proven identical through January experiment dates.

claims.claim: Treat DOI/date/copyright metadata and page-level primary text as different evidence classes in every LIRA score
claims.rationale: Archival catalog certifies item date but not detailed experimental wording; original text supports content within its edition.
claims.falsifier: Complete item-level provenance establishes primary facsimile independently.

claims.claim: Faraday Second Series §§231 and 242 retract the need to posit a separate electro-tonic state on the experimental grounds then available
claims.rationale: Contemporary text directly states previous grounds no longer justify this special state, while still allowing an unspecified future effect.
claims.falsifier: Different version of contemporary paragraph contradicts claim; reading must not infer metaphysical inexistence.

claims.claim: Faraday completely and permanently abandoned all electro-tonic-state concepts in 1832
claims.rationale: Direct historical 1832 withdrawal is scoped and major secondary scholarship describes later resumption; do not collapse transient withdrawal into permanent elimination.
claims.falsifier: Later original writings showing sustained repudiation with no later use would be needed; existing scholarship is contrary.

claims.claim: Second Series §§243–246 specify a discriminating arrangement in which same versus opposite magnetic poles imply contrasting apparatus behavior
claims.rationale: Original author's experiments compare rotation-induced current explanation with induced-magnetism explanation via opposed poles.
claims.falsifier: Contemporary original figures, equations or later replication challenge the claimed directional alternative.

claims.claim: The 1832 electro-tonic-state episode is a universal proof of formal language expansion or scientific paradigm law
claims.rationale: An author's revised physical explanation is not proof of any unique, universal rule for question-grammar changes.
claims.falsifier: A cross-domain formal and empirical discriminator surviving powerful existing rivals would be necessary.

claims.claim: Maintain Faraday as Q3/Q4/Q7 case including temporary withdrawal and renewed concepts, not only discovery success
claims.rationale: Historical record offers dated changes in explanatory commitments and severe rival test; already addressed extensively in existing history of science.
claims.falsifier: New first-hand source reveals the concepts were not actually revised or relevance to project removed.

claims.claim: Require line-by-line recognition of pre-1932 manuscript, published 1832 text, late retrospective revisions when assigning LIRA evidence
claims.rationale: New precise textual example and prior-art caution demand publication-version provenance to avoid conceptual finality error.
claims.falsifier: Variant collation demonstrates documented passages and interpretations are identical in all dated versions.

claims.claim: Faraday in a 29 Nov 1831 letter explicitly coined electro-tonic state for experimentally puzzling induction processes
claims.rationale: First-person contemporaneous formulation; not an already matured 1850s field ontology.
claims.falsifier: Autograph letter differs from critical transcription.

claims.claim: Faraday 1852 revisited electro-tonic state as candidate physical character of magnetic lines while acknowledging insufficient evidence
claims.rationale: Same term explicitly appears in §§3256 and 3269 with conditional physical-existence language.
claims.falsifier: Check original 1852 final journal facsimile or author notebook contrary wording.

claims.claim: Maxwell 1855/56 mathematically develops electro-tonic functions without claiming a corresponding material mechanism is experimentally established
claims.rationale: His own author text separates formal utility and proof of physical substratum.
claims.falsifier: Locate 1855 submitted manuscript or original printed issue claiming physical confirmation.

claims.claim: Maxwell 1861-62 mechanical vortices are acknowledged by author as provisional, not experimentally verified molecular reality
claims.rationale: Author explicitly notes provisional and temporary mechanical device, possible mathematically coincident rival mechanisms.
claims.falsifier: Full author statement showing unconditional physical certainty.

claims.claim: Faraday's 1831 electro-tonic physical state is strictly identical to Maxwell 1855 components and all modern gauge-potential meanings
claims.rationale: Connotations and representation change; labels and mathematical symbols alone establish no ontic identity.
claims.falsifier: Original mathematical and physical isomorphism with verified empirical bridge would be needed.

claims.claim: Faraday-to-Maxwell trajectory uniquely establishes a universal rule of creation of previously unthinkable scientific questions
claims.rationale: Historical case is strong cross-author process example but sophisticated prior historiography and no independent prospective discriminator.
claims.falsifier: Rival theory/experimentation can be separated with dated independent predictive test in several sciences.

claims.claim: Prioritize source-native Maxwell 1855/56 equations and gauges rather than unbounded new illustrative models
claims.rationale: Original mathematical definitions encode what changed across scientific traditions, and OCR equations are not yet visually verified.
claims.falsifier: Equation-image corroboration and original printed version could show current reading false.

claims.claim: Treat Faraday→Maxwell as bounded science-language transfer case, NOT independent alien science and not proof of unique ontic referents
claims.rationale: Shared empirical induction and inherited vocabulary enable transfer; genuinely alien reference systems lack these bridges.
claims.falsifier: Find genuinely independent scientific traditions with experimentally learned reference bridge.

claims.claim: Continue preserving all seven Q branches while using E/C/L to scope concept-reuse witnesses
claims.rationale: Founding program protects Q2/Q7 from source-ready mathematical-history tunnel vision.
claims.falsifier: Full constitutional review changes seven founding commitments.

warning: E02/E11 and E04/E14 are overlapping sources and do not count as independent corroborations. C12 asserts need to collate, not proof of exact edit timing. E13/E17/E18 share the same 1832 primary published document; cannot count as 3 independent witnesses. Attributed claim of temporary withdrawal has secondary historical support and is not a claim of permanent abandonment. E23 is reprinted primary text (Niven) and mathematical symbols are OCR-degraded; E24 is author text in a later paper, not independent confirmation of field realism. E25 only search excerpt.
